lines.text: A draw plate stretches gold into thread.
It is a steel plate with a row of tapered holes.
A jeweler points the wire and pulls it through one hole.
Then a smaller hole, and a smaller one after that.
Pulling hardens the metal, so it is heated every few holes.
For much of antiquity, gold wire was not drawn at all.

lines.text: Jewelers cut strips from hammered sheet and twisted them.

One gram of gold can make hundreds of meters of wire.

post.caption: A draw plate stretches gold into thread. It is a steel plate with a row of tapered holes. A jeweler points the wire and pulls it through one hole. Then a smaller hole, and a smaller one after that. Pulling hardens the metal, so it is heated every few holes. For much of antiquity, gold wire was not drawn at all. Jewelers cut strips from hammered sheet and twisted them. The earliest written description of a draw plate comes from the 1100s. The finest wire is drawn through a hole in a single diamond. One gram of gold can make hundreds of meters of wire.
